---
title: "About"
description: "Statistician and data scientist with a time series background, working in R and Python."
---

I'm Jeison, a statistician from Cali, Colombia. I studied statistics at Universidad del Valle, and my thesis compared ways of estimating the fractional differencing parameter in long-memory time series. I have stayed interested in time series ever since: ARIMA and GARCH models, state-space models, Kalman filters and Gaussian processes.

After my degree I joined CIAT, the International Center for Tropical Agriculture, where I spent six years on climate and agriculture. I modelled how climate change could affect crops across Latin America, ran crop simulations from R, and worked on the statistical models behind AClimate Colombia's seasonal forecasts. As part of CIAT's climate services team I shared in a UNFCCC Momentum for Change award in 2017, and the work led to papers in journals such as *Climate Services*, *Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution* and *Computers and Electronics in Agriculture*.

In 2020 and 2021 I taught time series and probability at Universidad del Valle and fundamentals of statistics at Universidad Católica. I have also co-directed an undergraduate thesis on the spectral analysis of cumbia, which is as much fun as it sounds.

Since 2021 I've worked at Globant on machine learning for customers in several industries: churn, segmentation, pricing, forecasting and recommendation. I led the data science on the DirecTV account, including the churn model, the segmentation and the marketing campaign work behind them. I currently work as an AI engineer at Globant, with Disney as the client, where I lead parts of the agent design on LLM systems.

## What I like working on

- Forecasting and filtering: state-space models, Kalman filters, structural time series
- Spatial and climate data
- Getting a model out of a notebook and into something other people rely on
- Deciding which steps of an LLM system should stay deterministic, and how to check its output

## What I write about

Tutorials in R and Python on statistics and data science, deep learning, AI engineering and data engineering, starting with time series. Posts with code link to a repository you can clone and run. They're on the [blog](blog/index.qmd).
